topic.title: Risk Minimization, Surrogate Losses, and Noisy Supervision
topic.overview: Learning algorithms usually optimize a convenient loss rather than the exact error users care about. This topic studies when that substitution is justified, how noise changes the answer, and how bias, variance, rejection, or distillation affect prediction risk. Guarantees depend on both the loss and the structure of the data-generating problem.
topic.whyItMatters: A well-behaved optimization objective is not enough if its minimizer makes poor decisions under the desired evaluation metric. Connecting surrogate losses to prediction risk helps explain when familiar classifiers tolerate corrupted labels and when additional assumptions or alternative objectives are necessary.
topic.evolution: Early work in 1991 contrasts empirical and structural risk minimization. Later studies develop calibrated surrogates and noise-aware classification. A 2020 result establishes error resistance under margin and distributional conditions; a 2026 ridge-regression analysis characterizes how optimally mixing teacher predictions with labels can improve squared prediction risk at nonstationary regularization levels.
openQuestions: Which surrogate guarantees remain informative under realistic mixtures of labeling errors?
How can distillation parameters be selected without optimistic reuse of evaluation data?

papers.title: Risk Monotonicity in Statistical Learning
papers.tldr: The paper constructs consistent algorithms with high-probability risk monotonicity and shows this property need not worsen excess-risk rates.

papers.title: Stability and Generalization of Bilevel Programming in Hyperparameter Optimization
papers.tldr: Stability-based bounds explain validation overfitting in bilevel hyperparameter optimization and show how regularization can reduce it.

papers.title: Surrogate Regret Bounds for Polyhedral Losses
papers.tldr: Polyhedral surrogates admit linear regret transfer, while sufficiently non-polyhedral surrogates incur a square-root relationship that slows target rates.

papers.title: Towards optimally abstaining from prediction with OOD test examples
papers.tldr: A transductive abstention method provides optimal loss guarantees that account explicitly for distribution shift and the cost of declining predictions.

papers.title: Unifying lower bounds on prediction dimension of convex surrogates
papers.tldr: The d-flats tool unifies and strengthens lower bounds on the prediction dimension required by consistent convex surrogates.

papers.title: Agnostic Learnability of Halfspaces via Logistic Loss
papers.tldr: The paper establishes logistic regression's worst-case classification limit and shows how an extra hinge-loss optimization step overcomes it.

papers.title: Being Properly Improper
papers.tldr: Twist-proper losses aim to recover clean label probabilities from distorted data, with an extended alpha-loss showing theoretical and empirical benefits.

papers.title: Consistent Polyhedral Surrogates for Top-k Classification and Variants
papers.tldr: The paper explains which top-k variants existing convex surrogates solve and constructs a consistent polyhedral surrogate for top-k classification.

papers.title: Decision-Focused Learning: Through the Lens of Learning to Rank
papers.tldr: Viewing decision-focused learning as ranking feasible solutions yields differentiable losses and practical runtime control with competitive empirical decision quality.

papers.title: Fisher SAM: Information Geometry and Sharpness Aware Minimisation
papers.tldr: Fisher SAM uses information-geometric neighborhoods to measure sharpness and improves performance on the evaluated benchmarks.

papers.title: Fishr: Invariant Gradient Variances for Out-of-Distribution Generalization
papers.tldr: Fishr matches gradient variances across training domains, locally aligning their loss landscapes and improving out-of-distribution performance in the reported evaluations.

papers.title: Fluctuations, Bias, Variance & Ensemble of Learners: Exact Asymptotics for Convex Losses in High-Dimension
papers.tldr: A high-dimensional theory characterizes correlated learners jointly, enabling analysis of ensemble error, statistical fluctuations, and double descent.

papers.title: Generic Coreset for Scalable Learning of Monotonic Kernels: Logistic Regression, Sigmoid and more
papers.tldr: Small coresets are impossible for some general monotonic losses, but regularization and an additional assumption enable efficient generic constructions.

papers.title: H-Consistency Bounds for Surrogate Loss Minimizers
papers.tldr: H-consistency bounds quantify how surrogate-loss errors translate into target errors for specified hypothesis classes.

papers.title: Learning General Halfspaces with Adversarial Label Noise via Online Gradient Descent
papers.tldr: Online gradient descent learns general halfspaces under Gaussian inputs and adversarial label noise with near-optimal guarantees.

papers.title: Model Agnostic Sample Reweighting for Out-of-Distribution Learning
papers.tldr: MAPLE searches for training-sample weights that improve out-of-distribution generalization, with linear-case theory separating generalization complexity from model size.

papers.title: Neural Fisher Discriminant Analysis: Optimal Neural Network Embeddings in Polynomial Time
papers.tldr: Neural Fisher Discriminant Analysis reformulates optimal two-layer discriminant embeddings as a convex problem solvable to global optimality.

papers.title: Sample Efficient Learning of Predictors that Complement Humans
papers.tldr: The paper develops theory and active learning methods for predictors that complement human experts and learn when to defer.

papers.title: Supervised Learning with General Risk Functionals
papers.tldr: Uniform control of loss distributions supports generalization guarantees and optimization methods for a broad family of risk-sensitive learning objectives.

papers.title: When AUC meets DRO: Optimizing Partial AUC for Deep Learning with Non-Convex Convergence Guarantee
papers.tldr: Distributionally robust formulations enable gradient-based partial-AUC optimization with exact non-smooth or approximate smooth objectives and convergence guarantees.

papers.title: Approximation with CNNs in Sobolev Space: with Applications to Classification
papers.tldr: New finite-network approximation bounds explain how CNN classification can avoid the curse of dimensionality when inputs lie near a low-dimensional manifold.

papers.title: Beyond the Return: Off-policy Function Estimation under User-specified Error-measuring Distributions
papers.tldr: Flexible regularization enables off-policy function-estimation guarantees under realizability while allowing users to choose how estimation error is weighted.

papers.title: Decision-Focused Learning without Decision-Making: Learning Locally Optimized Decision Losses
papers.tldr: Automatically learned, task-informed losses replace the optimization component of decision-focused training and outperform compared approaches on three resource allocation problems.

papers.title: Domain Generalization without Excess Empirical Risk
papers.tldr: The method optimizes a domain-generalization penalty while constraining empirical risk to remain optimal.

papers.title: Generalization Bounds with Minimal Dependency on Hypothesis Class via Distributionally Robust Optimization
papers.tldr: The paper derives distributionally robust generalization bounds that depend on the true loss and ambiguity-set structure rather than other candidate hypotheses.

papers.title: Generalizing Consistent Multi-Class Classification with Rejection to be Compatible with Arbitrary Losses
papers.tldr: Recasting rejection as an additional class enables flexible loss functions with explicit error bounds and conditions for consistent learning.

papers.title: Learning from Stochastically Revealed Preference
papers.tldr: Bayesian methods infer utility-distribution parameters from agents' choices under two stochastic preference models, with theoretical recovery guarantees.

papers.title: Multi-Class $H$-Consistency Bounds
papers.tldr: The paper establishes multiclass surrogate-to-target error bounds for restricted hypothesis sets and identifies cases where useful bounds are impossible.

papers.title: On Leave-One-Out Conditional Mutual Information For Generalization
papers.tldr: Leave-one-out conditional mutual information yields easier-to-compute generalization bounds that are non-vacuous on evaluated image-classification tasks.

papers.title: Post-hoc estimators for learning to defer to an expert
papers.tldr: Training a deferral rule after the base model helps balance predicted error against expert cost and addresses weaknesses in existing losses.

papers.title: Statistical Learning and Inverse Problems: A Stochastic Gradient Approach
papers.tldr: The paper establishes statistical guarantees for stochastic-gradient solutions to linear inverse problems and improves empirical performance through gradient smoothing.

papers.title: The Missing Invariance Principle found -- the Reciprocal Twin of Invariant Risk Minimization
papers.tldr: MRI reverses IRM's conditioning to enforce a complementary invariance, with conditional linear guarantees and strong nonlinear experimental results.

papers.title: Wasserstein Logistic Regression with Mixed Features
papers.tldr: The paper makes distributionally robust logistic regression tractable for mixed numerical and categorical features and reports improved benchmark performance.

papers.title: What is a Good Metric to Study Generalization of Minimax Learners?
papers.tldr: The primal gap addresses failures of existing minimax generalization metrics and supports new bounds in nonconvex-concave settings.

papers.title: Cross-Entropy Loss Functions: Theoretical Analysis and Applications
papers.tldr: Tight guarantees connect cross-entropy-like training losses to classification error and motivate new losses with reported adversarial robustness gains.

papers.title: Fast Excess Risk Rates via Offset Rademacher Complexity
papers.tldr: Offset Rademacher complexity provides a unified route to fast excess-risk bounds without requiring the Bernstein condition.

papers.title: Finite-Sample Analysis of Learning High-Dimensional Single ReLU Neuron
papers.tldr: Sharp risk bounds for GLM-tron and conditional negative results for SGD favor GLM-tron in the studied high-dimensional ReLU regression settings.

papers.title: Fundamental Tradeoffs in Learning with Prior Information
papers.tldr: Prioritized risk provides tools for proving learning limits when a learner’s prior information may be inaccurate.

papers.title: LegendreTron: Uprising Proper Multiclass Loss Learning
papers.tldr: LegendreTron jointly learns proper losses and multiclass probabilities using a multidimensional extension of monotonic link learning.

papers.title: Maximum Optimality Margin: A Unified Approach for Contextual Linear Programming and Inverse Linear Programming
papers.tldr: Maximum optimality margin learns from observed optimal decisions using a loss derived from downstream linear-program optimality conditions.

papers.title: Multicalibration as Boosting for Regression
papers.tldr: A shared algorithm links multicalibration and regression boosting, with Bayes-optimality guarantees governed by a necessary and sufficient weak learning condition.

papers.title: Statistical Learning under Heterogeneous Distribution Shift
papers.tldr: For additive predictors, theory and experiments link greater resilience to distribution shifts concentrated in features modeled by simpler function classes.

papers.title: Tilted Sparse Additive Models
papers.tldr: Tilted sparse additive models adjust the influence of individual losses to support robust, imbalanced, and multiobjective learning.

papers.title: A Unified Framework for Rank-based Loss Minimization
papers.tldr: A unified optimization framework handles multiple rank-based training objectives, with conditional convergence guarantees and supporting experiments.

papers.title: Agnostically Learning Single-Index Models using Omnipredictors
papers.tldr: The paper gives agnostic learning guarantees for single-index models with unknown monotone Lipschitz activations under bounded-second-moment assumptions.

papers.title: An Information Theory Perspective on Variance-Invariance-Covariance Regularization
papers.tldr: An information-theoretic analysis explains VICReg’s objective, establishes a generalization bound, and motivates improved self-supervised methods.

papers.title: Certified Minimax Unlearning with Generalization Rates and Deletion Capacity
papers.tldr: A minimax-specific Newton update with calibrated Gaussian noise enables certified unlearning with improved deletion capacity over the stated privacy-based baseline.

papers.title: $H$-Consistency Bounds: Characterization and Extensions
papers.tldr: The paper develops general, tighter guarantees connecting surrogate-loss error to classification error within specified hypothesis classes.

papers.title: In Defense of Softmax Parametrization for Calibrated and Consistent Learning to Defer
papers.tldr: An asymmetric loss makes softmax-based learning to defer statistically consistent while avoiding unbounded probability estimates.

papers.title: New Bounds for Hyperparameter Tuning of Regression Problems Across Instances
papers.tldr: The paper proves tight complexity bounds for linear regression regularization tuning and introduces a first learning guarantee for the logistic regression case.

papers.title: Regression with Cost-based Rejection
papers.tldr: For squared-error regression, the Bayes-optimal rejection rule compares target variance with rejection cost, and a surrogate loss can recover it under consistency conditions.

papers.title: Resilient Constrained Learning
papers.tldr: Resilient constrained learning adapts training requirements by balancing the performance benefits of relaxation against user-defined costs.

papers.title: Structured Prediction with Stronger Consistency Guarantees
papers.tldr: New structured-prediction surrogate losses provide non-asymptotic consistency bounds that account for the learner’s hypothesis class.

papers.title: Two-Stage Learning to Defer with Multiple Experts
papers.tldr: The paper develops theoretically consistent losses for learning which expert should receive an input after a predictor is trained.

papers.title: Understanding Contrastive Learning via Distributionally Robust Optimization
papers.tldr: A distributionally robust view explains contrastive learning's sampling-bias tolerance and motivates an adjusted InfoNCE loss.

papers.title: Agnostic Learning of Mixed Linear Regressions with EM and AM Algorithms
papers.tldr: With separation and good initialization, EM and alternating minimization can learn mixed linear regressions without assuming a mixture-generating model.

papers.title: Bridging Mini-Batch and Asymptotic Analysis in Contrastive Learning: From InfoNCE to Kernel-Based Losses
papers.tldr: A conditional analysis links contrastive losses through hyperspherical energy and motivates objectives with improved empirical performance and reduced dimensionality collapse.

papers.title: Criterion Collapse and Loss Distribution Control
papers.tldr: The paper identifies conditions where different learning criteria collapse into error-probability minimization and where non-monotonic alternatives can avoid that collapse.

papers.title: Data-Efficient Learning via Clustering-Based Sensitivity Sampling: Foundation Models and Beyond
papers.tldr: Clustering-based sensitivity sampling selects small training subsets with conditional loss guarantees and strong reported performance across applications.

papers.title: Domain Generalisation via Imprecise Learning
papers.tldr: Imprecise Domain Generalisation trains across a spectrum of risk preferences so operators can choose their generalization strategy at deployment.

papers.title: Exploiting Human-AI Dependence for Learning to Defer
papers.tldr: Accounting for dependence between a model and a human expert yields a new optimality formulation and improved learning-to-defer objective.

papers.title: $H$-Consistency Guarantees for Regression
papers.tldr: Under symmetry and boundedness assumptions, new H-consistency results distinguish regression surrogates and motivate algorithms for adversarial regression.

papers.title: Invariant Risk Minimization Is A Total Variation Model
papers.tldr: The paper interprets IRM through total variation and develops an L1-based alternative with broader function classes and competitive benchmark performance.

papers.title: On the Asymptotic Distribution of the Minimum Empirical Risk
papers.tldr: The paper broadens asymptotic theory for minimum empirical risk and derives tools for confidence sets and hypothesis testing.

papers.title: Optimal Ridge Regularization for Out-of-Distribution Prediction
papers.tldr: The paper characterizes optimal ridge regularization under distribution shifts, including conditions where negative regularization is best.

papers.title: Regression with Multi-Expert Deferral
papers.tldr: A regression framework learns when to defer to multiple experts, with surrogate objectives backed by hypothesis-specific consistency guarantees.

papers.title: Stability Evaluation through Distributional Perturbation Analysis
papers.tldr: The proposed stability criterion measures the smallest distributional perturbation needed to cause a specified increase in risk.

papers.title: Towards Generalization beyond Pointwise Learning: A Unified Information-theoretic Perspective
papers.tldr: A unified information-theoretic framework bounds generalization for learning objectives involving individual examples, pairs, and larger groups.

papers.title: Understanding the Impact of Introducing Constraints at Inference Time on Generalization Error
papers.tldr: For certain multiclass losses, including softmax cross-entropy, inference-time constraints do not increase the generalization-error gap relative to the best model.

papers.title: A Universal Growth Rate for Learning with Smooth Surrogate Losses
papers.tldr: The paper establishes square-root error-bound growth for several smooth classification losses and identifies minimizability gaps as a key factor distinguishing them.

papers.title: Cardinality-Aware Set Prediction and Top-$k$ Classification
papers.tldr: Cardinality-aware classification learns to balance prediction accuracy against the number of labels returned, with supporting consistency bounds and experiments.

papers.title: Constrained Binary Decision Making
papers.tldr: A unified mathematical framework characterizes optimal strategies for a broad range of constrained binary decision problems.

papers.title: Controlling Multiple Errors Simultaneously with a PAC-Bayes Bound
papers.tldr: A new PAC-Bayes bound controls multiple error probabilities together, implicitly covering every weighting of those errors.

papers.title: Decision-Focused Learning with Directional Gradients
papers.tldr: Perturbation Gradient losses support gradient-based decision-aware training with asymptotic best-in-class guarantees even under model misspecification.

papers.title: Derandomizing Multi-Distribution Learning
papers.tldr: Removing randomness from multi-distribution predictors can be computationally hard, but a structural condition enables efficient conversion.

papers.title: Error Analysis of Spherically Constrained Least Squares Reformulation in Solving the Stackelberg Prediction Game
papers.tldr: The paper derives and experimentally validates an estimation-error analysis for the SCLS method used in least-squares Stackelberg prediction games.

papers.title: Implicit Bias of Mirror Flow on Separable Data
papers.tldr: Under stated loss and potential assumptions, mirror flow on separable data converges in direction to a maximum-margin classifier determined by the potential’s horizon function.

papers.title: Information-theoretic Limits of Online Classification with Noisy Labels
papers.tldr: The Hellinger separation of noisy label distributions characterizes minimax online classification risk up to a logarithmic hypothesis-class factor.

papers.title: Learning a Single Neuron Robustly to Distributional Shifts and Adversarial Label Noise
papers.tldr: A primal-dual algorithm learns a single neuron with a constant-factor squared-error guarantee under a chi-squared-penalized adversarial distribution objective.

papers.title: Learning with Fitzpatrick Losses
papers.tldr: Fitzpatrick losses provide tighter alternatives to Fenchel-Young losses while preserving their prediction links and separate convexity.

papers.title: Localized Adaptive Risk Control
papers.tldr: L-ARC adapts prediction-set thresholds locally to support subpopulation risk guarantees while preserving worst-case control and exposing a convergence trade-off.

papers.title: On the Efficiency of ERM in Feature Learning
papers.tldr: Under stated conditions, empirical risk minimization that learns a feature map approaches the excess-risk behavior of an oracle that already knows the best map.

papers.title: Realizable $H$-Consistent and Bayes-Consistent Loss Functions for Learning to Defer
papers.tldr: The paper develops surrogate losses for learning to defer and proves multiple consistency guarantees under specified conditions, including results for general costs.

papers.title: Regression under demographic parity constraints via unlabeled post-processing
papers.tldr: A theoretically grounded post-processing method targets demographic parity using unlabeled data and accurate predictors, without sensitive attributes at inference.

papers.title: Rejection via Learning Density Ratios
papers.tldr: The framework decides when a pretrained classifier should abstain by comparing the data distribution with an idealized distribution favoring its performance.

papers.title: Soft ascent-descent as a stable and flexible alternative to flooding
papers.tldr: SoftAD smooths flooding's ascent-descent updates, achieving competitive accuracy with smaller reported loss generalization gaps and model norms.

papers.title: The Implicit Bias of Gradient Descent on Separable Multiclass Data
papers.tldr: A multiclass exponential-tail condition extends implicit-bias theory for gradient descent beyond cross-entropy on separable data.

papers.title: Trading off Consistency and Dimensionality of Convex Surrogates for Multiclass Classification
papers.tldr: The paper studies conditional guarantees for compact convex surrogates and a parallel construction that recovers full consistency across multiple instances.

papers.title: A Generalization Result for Convergence in Learning-to-Optimize
papers.tldr: A probabilistic framework establishes high-probability convergence to critical points for learned optimizers across parameterized loss families.

papers.title: A Versatile Influence Function for Data Attribution with Non-Decomposable Loss
papers.tldr: VIF extends efficient training-data attribution to coupled loss functions, closely matching leave-one-out retraining in three evaluated applications.

papers.title: Contextual Optimization Under Model Misspecification: A Tractable and Generalizable Approach
papers.tldr: An integrated learning-and-optimization framework uses a tractable surrogate loss to improve decisions under model misspecification.

papers.title: Exactly Tight Information-theoretic Generalization Bounds via Binary Jensen-Shannon Divergence
papers.tldr: Binary Jensen-Shannon divergence yields exactly tight generalization bounds for randomized learning with bounded losses, without added stability or compressibility assumptions.

papers.title: Generalization and Robustness of the Tilted Empirical Risk
papers.tldr: The paper establishes conditional generalization and robustness guarantees for negative-tilt empirical risk and uses the bounds to guide tilt selection.

papers.title: Loss Functions and Operators Generated by f-Divergences
papers.tldr: A framework generates convex alternatives to cross-entropy from f-divergences, with an efficient operator algorithm and promising language-model results.

papers.title: Mastering Multiple-Expert Routing: Realizable $H$-Consistency and Strong Guarantees for Learning to Defer
papers.tldr: New surrogate losses provide theoretical guarantees for routing inputs among experts while balancing prediction accuracy and computational cost.

papers.title: Model Steering: Learning with a Reference Model Improves Generalization Bounds and Scaling Laws
papers.tldr: DRRho provides a theoretical framework for reference-guided training and improves the reported generalization, efficiency, and scaling of CLIP.

papers.title: Principled Algorithms for Optimizing Generalized Metrics in Binary Classification
papers.tldr: METRO converts generalized classification metrics into cost-sensitive learning objectives with hypothesis-class-aware and finite-sample guarantees.

papers.title: Relating Misfit to Gain in Weak-to-Strong Generalization Beyond the Squared Loss
papers.tldr: The paper extends misfit-based weak-to-strong performance theory to Bregman losses and classification, with convexity assumptions or mixtures of strong models.

papers.title: Robust Automatic Modulation Classification with Fuzzy Regularization
papers.tldr: FR-AMC improves radio modulation classification by incorporating prediction ambiguity, adaptive sample weighting, and class separation into training.

papers.title: Connecting Jensen–Shannon and Kullback–Leibler Divergences: A New Bound for Representation Learning
papers.tldr: A new divergence bound explains how Jensen–Shannon objectives can increase a guaranteed lower bound on mutual information.

papers.title: Consistency Conditions for Differentiable Surrogate Losses
papers.tldr: The paper establishes simpler calibration tests for differentiable surrogate losses, with guarantees that depend on dimension and convexity.

papers.title: How to Learn a Star: Binary Classification with Starshaped Polyhedral Sets
papers.tldr: The paper characterizes the expressive capacity and loss geometry of classifiers with starshaped polyhedral decision boundaries.

papers.title: Implicit Bias of Spectral Descent and Muon on Multiclass Separable Data
papers.tldr: On separable multiclass linear problems, Spectral Descent and Muon converge toward spectral-norm max-margin classifiers.

papers.title: Is the acquisition worth the cost? Surrogate losses for Consistent Two-stage Classifiers
papers.tldr: The paper derives a trainable surrogate with a consistency guarantee for jointly learning when to classify and when to purchase additional features.

papers.title: Learning from Interval Targets
papers.tldr: The paper develops generalization bounds and a worst-case training formulation for regression with interval-valued labels.

papers.title: Multiclass Loss Geometry Matters for Generalization of Gradient Descent in Separable Classification
papers.tldr: For separable multiclass linear classification, loss-template geometry determines sharply different class-count dependence in gradient descent's generalization bounds.

papers.title: On the sample complexity of semi-supervised multi-objective learning
papers.tldr: The paper identifies when unlabeled data can absorb the complexity cost of multi-objective learning and when that cost remains unavoidable.

papers.title: Optimal and Provable Calibration in High-Dimensional Binary Classification: Angular Calibration and Platt Scaling
papers.tldr: Angular calibration provides provably calibrated and Bregman-optimal predictions in a Gaussian high-dimensional setting, with conditional guarantees for Platt scaling.

papers.title: Robustly Learning Monotone Single-Index Models
papers.tldr: A vector-field-guided algorithm efficiently learns broad classes of monotone single-index models under Gaussian inputs and adversarial label noise.

papers.title: Smart Surrogate Losses for Contextual Stochastic Linear Optimization with Robust Constraints
papers.tldr: SPO-RC+ trains predictions for optimization with uncertain constraints using a feasibility-sensitive surrogate and bias-corrected data selection.

papers.title: Targeted Maximum Likelihood Learning: An Optimization Perspective
papers.tldr: An optimization and geometric analysis establishes conditional TMLE convergence, sufficient one-update criteria, and a previously unidentified overshooting phenomenon.

papers.title: When Does Curriculum Learning Help? A Theoretical Perspective
papers.tldr: A theoretical framework identifies sufficient conditions for curricula to improve generalization and connects them with practical training results.

papers.title: A Solver-Free Training Method for Predict-then-Optimize
papers.tldr: A theoretically supported surrogate trains decision-focused prediction models without solver calls, substantially reducing reported training costs.

papers.title: Bulk-Calibrated Credal Ambiguity Sets: Fast, Tractable Decision Making under Out-of-Sample Contamination
papers.tldr: Separating a learned high-probability region from a bounded tail makes contamination-aware robust optimization finite and tractable.

papers.title: Characterization of Gaussian Universality Breakdown in High-Dimensional Empirical Risk Minimization
papers.tldr: A heuristic analysis characterizes predictions as an approximately Gaussian fluctuation plus a potentially non-Gaussian mean contribution under stated assumptions.

papers.title: Generalization Bounds for Out-of-distribution Generalization
papers.tldr: Under RCS and empirical-RCS conditions, average source-domain risk minimization achieves a nearly optimal OOD error rate without estimating distributional discrepancies.

papers.title: Hard labels sampled from sparse targets mislead rotation invariant algorithms
papers.tldr: For sparse logistic targets with sampled hard labels, rotation-invariant algorithms have worse excess-risk rates than simple coordinate-sensitive alternatives.

papers.title: Improved Scaling Laws via Weak-to-Strong Generalization in Random Feature Ridge Regression
papers.tldr: In identified random-feature ridge-regression regimes, a student trained on weak labels can achieve a better error scaling law than its teacher.

papers.title: Linear-Core Surrogates: Smooth Loss Functions with Linear Rates for Classification and Structured Prediction
papers.tldr: Linear-Core Surrogates combine differentiable convex losses with linear consistency guarantees across classification and structured prediction.

papers.title: On the Accuracy of Newton Step and Influence Function Data Attributions
papers.tldr: Local curvature and smoothness conditions yield sharper attribution guarantees and explain when a Newton step outperforms influence functions.

papers.title: Optimal Unconstrained Self-Distillation in Ridge Regression: Strict Improvements, Precise Asymptotics, and One-Shot Tuning
papers.tldr: Optimally weighted self-distillation strictly improves ridge regression wherever teacher risk is nonstationary in regularization, and the optimal weight can be negative.

papers.title: Positive-Unlabeled Learning with Extreme Scarcity of Labeled Positives
papers.tldr: ScalePU targets two sources of risk-estimation uncertainty to improve positive-unlabeled learning when labeled positives are extremely scarce.

papers.title: Weak-to-Strong Generalization via Bregman Bias–Variance Decomposition
papers.tldr: A Bregman bias–variance analysis identifies conditions that favor students outperforming weaker teachers and motivates reverse cross-entropy training.
